name: vanilla
displayName: Vanilla JavaScript + Vite 8 (no framework · JSDoc + zod)
extractedFrom: newly created — no proven original. No other pack was opened, not even as a format reference (only assets/pack-resource-template.md was used)

exampleDomain.note: Every pack and every seam uses the same example domain. L0 issues the vocabulary policy (`vocab-task`) from this value so that the gate blocks divergence — measured, the frontend used /tasks and the backend /notes, and the complete examples could not run against each other

fixesVariantsNote: **The language is the whole of this pack.** The preset leaves the default at JavaScript, and that choice replaces the type-standard slot with **JSDoc + runtime schema validation** — a project that picks TypeScript gets that slot back, so this pack hands it not a variant but **the wrong thing**. Routing is pinned to a **single History API entry point**: choose multiple HTML entry points and the whole account of the router·state restoration·link interception becomes meaningless (it turns into a question about Vite's multi-input configuration). The bundler is Vite — `import.meta.env` and the module resolution rules are premises of the body text
pkgsNote: **`typescript` is not the language this pack ships but its checker.** tsc with `checkJs` on reads JSDoc comments as types and checks them — that is the only device that actually enforces this axis's type-standard slot. `pack-smoke.sh --online` installs only `pkgs`, so without it here the typecheck stays a skip, and **that skip is not a pass but an absence of checking**. Measured (2026-08-24): with `allowJs` alone, a planted JSDoc type error still came out as a typecheck pass. `happy-dom` is Vitest's DOM environment — lighter than jsdom, and it covers the surface this pack uses (DOM·events·History)

runtime.browsers: browsers with native support for ES2022 modules (Vite's default target)

runtimeNote: the runtime environment, not an npm dependency
notesLanguage: This pack has no `dataLayerPolicyEngine` — that value is **a property of the backend axis**, and the frontend axis only learns it at combination time. When the seam is generated, the backend pack's value has to be passed along with it, and in a combination where the value is `false` (a self-hosted server·DynamoDB and the like) an account saying the data layer backs it up gives exactly the opposite instruction

resources.nav: the JSDoc type convention and checkJs · zod schemas and re-validation at the boundary · validated environment values (config) · Vitest + happy-dom · what not to test
module-scope stores · subscribing and unsubscribing · derived values · the local vs global criterion · where not to use a store
the DOM-manipulation boundary · building with the template element · event delegation · extracting a shared component and the duty to search before creating one · the cleanup contract
CSS custom properties and @layer · the tokens a component owns · the class-name convention · the boundary where inline styles are banned
the History API router · link interception and modifier keys · where the protected route goes · return-path validation (safeReturnTo) · 404 and scroll restoration
the three states loading·empty·error · AbortController and races · retry and backoff · where not to do an optimistic update

seamSlotNotes.data-fetching: the actual API call·envelope parsing·cache. The envelope is a function of the wire contract, so the combination decides it, not the axis. **Two things the axis pins down**: ⓐ a response is not trusted input, so **parse it with zod at the boundary** (`TaskSchema.safeParse`) ⓑ cancellation goes through `AbortController` and that signal is handed to `createResource`
seamSlotNotes.auth-and-session: where the token·session is kept and how it is refreshed · the login/logout flow · the protected route's verdict. **The auth method is not a function of the axis** — the backend axis decides whether it is a session cookie or a bearer token. **The one thing the axis provides is `safeReturnTo`**, and the seam **must** pass the post-login return through it
seamSlotNotes.complete-example: schema → store → component → route → test, end to end

clusters.why: **This is the first pack of a new toolchain, so a pilot is mandatory.** The JSDoc convention and the zod schemas are premises of every other file, and the store's generic (`@template T`) is the hardest spot in JSDoc — whether tsc with `checkJs` on really checks that shape is confirmed here for the first time. Launch three clusters at once on top of a wrong convention and all of them get reverted
The design tokens a component owns span both files. The class-name convention and the form of DOM creation are the same decision
A route change has to cancel the request in flight, so the lifetime of `AbortController` is tied to the router's. The three-state render and the 404 render contend for the same container

knownGaps.detail: The authoring·verification environment has no browser. **DOM·events·History are verified by proxy with `happy-dom`** (the Vitest environment), and the real render·computed CSS values·scroll restoration·per-browser differences in `popstate` cannot be run against the real thing. Each tag records how far the proxy reaches

knownGaps.what: machine policies aimed at the seam are judged only after assembly
knownGaps.detail: The target files only exist once there is a seam. `--pack` reports them explicitly as deferred to after assembly, and once `install-guide.sh` has assembled, `--guide --assembly` renders the verdict
